evidence.detail: Static decompressor operates over one shared rs/x/b state object and implements BZip2 bit/Huffman/block decode stages.
StreamLoader invokes this class when packed and unpacked archive lengths differ.
Classic client BZip2Decompressor exposes the same static byte-array decompress entrypoint and shared state-machine organization.

proposals.note: BZip2Decompressor is fixed by exact algorithm and archive-loader use.

evidence.detail: State object holds BZip2 input/output positions, 256/257 symbol tables, 16 group flags, selector arrays, six Huffman tables, decode limits/bases/permutations and block counters.
BZip2Decompressor mutates this object throughout decompression and keeps one static instance.
Layout matches the classic client's dedicated BZip2 decoder state/context object.

proposals.note: BZip2State is the conservative semantic name for the exact decompressor state block.

evidence.detail: Class parses an archive header through Stream, supports GZIP or BZip2 whole-archive decompression, stores per-entry name hashes/sizes/offsets and retrieves entries by uppercased name hash.
Classic StreamLoader has the same archive arrays, hash*61 name lookup, constructor over archive bytes and getDataForName behavior.

proposals.note: StreamLoader follows the exact classic archive-loader structure.

evidence.detail: Class owns two 256-int arrays plus ISAAC accumulator/counter state and emits one pseudorandom int per call.
Initialization uses the golden-ratio constant -1640531527 and the standard ISAAC shift/mix sequence; generation uses the canonical 13,6,2,16 shifts.
Stream holds this type and adds its next value to outgoing opcodes.

proposals.note: IsaacCipher is fixed by the standard ISAAC algorithm and packet-opcode usage.

evidence.detail: Class extends R25 NodeSub and owns byte[] payload, byte offset/bit-position state, dozens of primitive/string/byte-array read-write transforms, RSA via BigInteger and an attached ISAAC generator.
All classic definition decoders in R28 consume this type; opcode write adds the next ISAAC value before storing the byte.
Classic 317 Stream has the same NodeSub inheritance, buffer/currentOffset/bitPosition layout, RSA transform and ISAAC-backed opcode write surface.

proposals.note: Stream follows the exact classic client stream/buffer architecture.
